name: binn
listed_description: Binary serialization format, meant to be compact, fast and easy-to-use.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README, spec.md and usage.md have no benchmark or msgpack mention (only design claims: sizes stored with elements, zero-copy reads of strings/blobs/containers); the repo has no benchmark directory (root: conversions, examples, fuzzing, src, test); issue search for msgpack returns 0 results; web searches found no third-party shootout including binn (the arXiv 2201.03051 JSON-compatible binary serialization benchmark does not include it). Directional claim only.

name: CGAL
listed_description: Collection of efficient and reliable geometric algorithms.
reason: No first-party numeric comparison against a named external baseline reachable. Checked CGAL manual sources in the repo (Triangulation_3, Spatial_searching, Convex_hull_2/3, Surface_mesh, Polygon_mesh_processing, Kernel_23, Mesh_3, Orthtree, Isosurfacing_3 and about 40 more) and Installation/CHANGES.md: the benchmarks there are CGAL against itself (kernels, sequential versus parallel, bucket sizes) or give no numbers (Orthtree 'faster than a kd-tree', Marching Cubes 'substantially faster' than Delaunay refinement, 'efficient'). Triangulation_3 manual points to Liu and Snoeyink MSRI 2005 benchmarks comparing CGAL to other 3D Delaunay software, but that paper could not be opened. Search snippets of VQhull (arXiv 2510.09417: CGAL Quickhull 0.61 s versus Qhull 1.1 s on a 10^7-point disk) and ParGeo are third-party papers with CGAL as one comparison row; arXiv is blocked here, so no page with those numbers was opened.

name: CPL
listed_description: The Common Pipeline Library; a set of libraries designed to be a comprehensive, efficient and robust software toolkit
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. www.eso.org is blocked by the egress proxy (EGRESS_BLOCKED), so the project pages could not be opened; a web search for CPL performance or benchmarks against CFITSIO, numpy or OpenCV returned only package listings (Fedora, Debian/Trisquel, Ubuntu) and the introduction text describing CPL as 'robust, fast and generic', which is a directional claim without numbers. CPL is distributed as tarballs from ESO, with no GitHub repo to read for benchmark code.
